_about: Design decisions made from variant boards (design doc: Execution plan > Decision workflow). One record per decision, appended, never rewritten once chosen. Every record is reported to Alex so it can be added to the design doc's decision log, which stays the source of truth; this file is what the build reads.

record_shape.area: the design doc area, e.g. Trees, Shadows, Walls, UI
record_shape.question: what was being decided, in one line
record_shape.board: variants/<id>/ -- the board the choice was made from; its seed and parameter sets are in that folder's board.json
record_shape.chosen: a variant name, 'blend of A and B', or 'new round'
record_shape.status: proposed | chosen by Alex | logged in design doc

decisions.question: How transparent should cast shadows be? (Alex: shadows need to be softer, meaning more transparent)
decisions.notes: Alex: 'default to D for now'. Open follow-up raised with it: whether shadows should darken as the sun climbs (a sun-elevation coupling); not decided.

decisions.question: The unit art mockup's proposals: side colours, where each side's colour goes, and how far a plane's shadow sits from it
decisions.board: reference/mockups/unit_sheet.html (a mockup sheet, not a variant board)
decisions.notes: Alex: 'I love the rest of the decisions. The accent colors are perfectly toned. Those might be useful colors to mirror in the HUD.' The pen line was left open (variants/pen-line/).

decisions.question: Should an ink line's width vary along it, and how?
options: C heavier on the shadow side
decisions.notes: Alex: 'Shadow side looks the best.' Factor values are the board's; tuning them is a later board.

decisions.question: The sandbox demo's baseline: map scale, turn length, steps, stalls, map edge, ready-up, empty plans, the minute of flight
decisions.board: none (a recommendation table in chat; the scale options came from Track T's and Track S's arithmetic)

parameters.stalls: none in the demo; later a stall may cost an altitude band
parameters.map_edge: the planner refuses a step that ends outside the map; the AI turns back on its own
parameters.ready_up: editing a plan after Ready un-readies that player; the turn plays when the last player is ready
parameters.empty_plan: the plane flies on straight at its current speed
parameters.minute_of_flight: a simulated minute (about 12 turns), which sizes the map at 5,000 m

decisions.notes: Alex: '1-7 look good'. The scale is a starting value: the demo exposes it as a live knob so Alex can decide by flying. Items 8 (how height reads in ink) and 9 (terrain level fills vs object fills) are still open.

decisions.question: How does height read in ink on the full render?
decisions.notes: Alex: 'I strongly prefer the contours visually but I am not sure what they are signaling.' Open with it: what line breaks mean, and whether height steps are passable to ground units.

decisions.question: How do object fills relate to the ground level they stand on?
options: today: ground +0.025 L per level, fills fixed
1: fills step up with the ground
decisions.notes: Alex: 'For ground level fill - I actually like the current look the most.' Accepted with it: on the top level, wall and rock fills sit slightly darker than the ground (-0.018 / -0.011 L).

decisions.question: Are height steps passable to ground units, and what do the contours signal?
options: A every step a cliff, crossed at ramps or roads
B every step a slope, crossed anywhere slower
C mixed: some edges cliffs, some slopes

parameters.rule: every height step is a cliff: impassable to ground units, crossed only at ramps or roads
parameters.contours: tightly packed at every step (a cliff); a gap in the lines marks a ramp
parameters.contour_breaks_now: none: lines drawn unbroken until ramps exist
parameters.ramp_shadows: when ramps are added, their shadows must be complete and correct (a ramp is a sloped surface: its shadow varies along it and meets the cliff's); no partial version

decisions.notes: Alex first chose C (mixed cliffs and slopes), then: 'Actually, I take that back. Lets do A.' Also: 'draw the lines unbroken for now'. Ramps come with roads and ground units. On ramps: 'The shadows are much more complex with ramps. I don't want to do them less then 100% when we add them.'
